column1: # The expected-difference list:  the differences between two corpus
# captures of one tree that are accounted for.  Read by `corpus-compare`
# (s3-tests-rs, src/bin/corpus-compare.rs;  the rules are
# s3_tests_rs::corpus::compare), which `standup.rs compare` runs.
# The diff gates:  a difference not matched by a row here fails the
# comparison.  That is the point -- a comparison whose negative case
# cannot occur proves nothing -- so every row is a claim that someone
# has to defend, and a row with no reason is not a row.
# Seven tab-separated columns:
#   pair      which two captures.  noobaa:unconverted is the NooBaa run
#             against the unconverted RGW run -- RGW over the tree after
#             `import`, each bucket's record imported and its objects as
#             NooBaa wrote them;  a difference no row accounts for is an
#             adoption defect.  unconverted:converted is that run against
#             the converted RGW run, after `adopt`;  a difference no row
#             accounts for is a conversion defect.
#   when      the modality this row applies in -- md5-off, md5-on, or
#             blank for both.  A modality is a property of the tree,
#             fixed when NooBaa wrote its objects, so the two are two
#             trees and one file covers both rather than two drifting.
#   artifact  manifest | inventory | run
#   subject   which subject the row is about:  `object <key>` or
#             `bucket <name>` for a manifest, a path for an inventory;
#             blank for any.  A row about one object must name it, or it
#             excuses the same difference on every object
#   key       manifest:  the field, third column
#             inventory: xattr:<name>, type, mode, owner, or size
#             run:       the stem whose artifact is absent entirely
#             `*` matches any run of characters, anywhere.  The first
#             row that matches a difference is the one that judges it.
#   class     each a statement about the one pair the row names:
#             equal      values must be identical
#             recognize:<r>  both values pass through normalizer <r>,
#                        then must be identical -- so the row still
#                        asserts both are the same *kind* of value
#             differs    values may differ
#             vanishes   present on the left, must be absent on the right
#             absent     present on one side only, either side
#             filtered   should never appear;  the writer drops it
#   reason    why, in one line.  Required.
# NEVER key a row on a literal value from their side.  Their ETag and
# version id embed an mtime whose low 8 bits are lost to a double in
# their C++ (fs_napi.cpp:360), one `int64_t` from being fixed;  a row
# that names the string breaks on their next release instead of
# failing honestly.  Key on the field.
# Rows marked PROVISIONAL were derived from the NooBaa capture plus the
# mapping in docs/NOOBAA_WRITE_SURFACE.md.  `capture/rgw` does not
# exist yet (C2b), so **no row here has been confirmed by an actual
# diff** and the first real run is expected to move some of them.  Four
# of twenty carry the mark;  the rest rest on a measurement or on code
# that was read for the purpose.
# ---- named objects, first because the first matching row judges -----
# `.noobaa-nsfs-k-under-temp` is a client's object whose name starts
# with NooBaa's temp prefix.  NooBaa stores it and its listing hides it
# -- the prefix it hides is wider than its temp directory,
# `.noobaa-nsfs_<bucket id>` -- and RGW lists it, which is correct
# (DECISIONS.md 2026-10-12).  The corpus asserts the RGW side in observe
# mode;  these rows account for NooBaa's.
noobaa:unconverted

column1: # ---- adoption:  what the ETag says, by modality ---------------------
# **nsfs never hashes an object on a read** (`ETAG_STRATEGY.md`).  An
# object this gateway did not write is answered with the `mtime-ino`
# token synthesized from its `statx`, per read, persisted nowhere --
# whatever `rgw_non_md5_etag` says, because that option governs what a
# *writer* digests.  NooBaa does the same thing for the same reason.
# So in md5-off both sides report a token;  in md5-on they stored a
# digest and we forward it.
noobaa:unconverted

column1: # One item, with no class asserted because it needs a measurement
# rather than an argument:
#   inventory  mode    C1 normalizes permissions and their files are
#       0660 in the capture.  What conversion writes has not been
#       measured against a tree they wrote.
# Kept so they are not re-raised.
#   version.mtime-<...>-ino-<...>.* field names **align**.  NooBaa
#       stores every version id in user.noobaa.version_id -- the
#       current version included -- and we forward the stored string
#       (NB_KEYS, xattr_strategy.cc:131) rather than recomputing it.
#       One tree, one set of ids, all three captures.
#   *.refused is **fixed in the generator**, not here:  the field is
#       emitted whether or not a configuration was refused, with
#       <none> where it was not, so a capability divergence is one
#       changed value rather than a removed line and an added one.
#       Same for log-target-policy, whose subject was a random bucket
#       name and is now derived.
#   the ETag a sideloaded object reports is a synthetic token on both
#       sides and in every configuration, because neither gateway
#       hashes an object it did not write -- nsfs synthesizes from the
#       statx on read (ETAG_STRATEGY.md), NooBaa does the same.  So the
#       md5-off rows above are about two tokens, never a token against
#       a digest.
